review.scope: Bounded hosted Git file-transport contention/recovery fixture and private stderr evidence; no live activation. Review fixture and existing diagnostic/ledger callers, source-only; original CI cause remains unknown.
findings: Fail-closed boundaries verified in source: verify() refuses before any mutation on a non-absolute or existing destination and on <512 MiB free capacity, matching the two refusal tests (which also confirm git_run is never invoked and existing bytes are preserved); all persistent artifacts (started.json, outcomes.json, summary.json, receipts, stderr captures) are created fresh under a 0700 root with umask 0o077, exclusive-open where it matters, and nothing is ever deleted or overwritten — a prior attempt directory blocks replay as documented.

Privacy holds: raw Git stderr goes only to 0600 files inside 0700 mkdtemp directories under the private diagnostics root; receipts record an argv SHA-256, not argv; invoke() records only error type and returncode; raised exceptions carry an opaque receipt name instead of arguments/stdout/stderr; result.stderr is blanked for callers; the stdout summary contains counts and hashes only. git_diagnostics rejects stdout/stderr/shell overrides and validates diagnostics-root ownership, mode 0700, non-symlink, and not-inside-a-checkout, failing closed on each.

Recovery and halt semantics are correct in _admit: the duplicate-key check precedes the halt check and returns without a CAS write, so a fresh client replays all eight admitted identities read-only (proved by the before==after pin comparison), and the halted check precedes day rollover, so the midnight event observes the latched halt with no automatic reset. Event identity binding (source/branch/kind) is re-verified on duplicate admission. Note deliberately: an already-admitted run_id:attempt replays as ADMITTED even after halt — intended deduplication, worth one explicit sentence in the ops doc.

Expected-count arithmetic checks out for N=4 over 24 distinct events: exactly 8 admissions with count 1..8, one N notice at 4 and one 2N notice at 8 (sequence==count, so notifications==2 exactly), halt latched at 8, remaining requests returned HALTED status (not errors). CAS verification is sound: force-with-lease with the exact old pin, porcelain single-status check bound to new+':'+REF, '=' treated as race, forced-update flag rejected, and the push-failure path correctly distinguishes a moved ref (retry) from write unavailability (raise), which is safe because the ref can only advance.

Authority preserved: the RATIFIED config is synthetic (operator_approval SYNTHETIC_ONLY) against a disposable local bare repository only; GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=file, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM/GLOBAL isolation, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and expected_remote pinning confine transport; agent identity is honestly attributed with an .invalid email; the remote-ledger OPERATOR_MUST_INITIALIZE_STATE_REF guard, operator-only reset/initialize, server-semantics gate and hosted-only main() gates are untouched. Note the fixture initializes the ledger via the local update-ref path, so the remote initialization guard itself is not exercised by this fixture.

Suggestion (doc accuracy): GIT_TRANSPORT_HOSTED_CHECK_20260907.md says 'eight independent clients'; the code creates 24 per-invocation client repositories driven by 8 worker threads, plus one recovery client. Small wording fix avoids misreading the concurrency shape.

Suggestion (fixture robustness, fail-closed only): read() fetches the pinned SHA after ls-remote; if another writer advances the ref in between, the pin is no longer an advertised tip and the fetch depends on protocol v2 permitting non-tip wants. Under a protocol v0 fallback (old git or GIT_PROTOCOL override) this surfaces as an invocation error and a false-negative run — no privacy or state impact, but worth knowing when interpreting a hosted failure.

Suggestion (diagnostics completeness): in git_diagnostics.run, only TimeoutExpired and OSError are caught around subprocess.run; any other exception skips receipt.json, leaving an orphan stderr capture that the summary's receipt-glob hash/mode verification never inspects. Consider writing the receipt in a finally block.

Observation for operator follow-up (recorded evidence, not introduced by this change): RESUME_RECONCILIATION_20260907.json shows research-system-handover.service ActiveState=active with User=root, which sits uneasily with the stated non-root runtime-role requirement; the reconciliation itself is read-only with zero retries/model calls as claimed.

Limits of this review: source-only, no execution performed and none claimed; orchestrator.git_publication.scan_commit (imported inside GitLedger.cas) was not in the supplied bundle and is unverified; the ops doc's local-probe pass (947 receipts, base a94d886) is correctly labeled uncommitted-fixture evidence, and the original CI fetch exit-128 cause remains unknown — a passing fixture cannot identify it, as the doc honestly states.
